R3A-bear-backcountry-0003.name: 150 m N of Fiftyseven Creek
R3A-bear-backcountry-0003.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R3A-bear-backcountry-0003.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2012 (14 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SE facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Fiftyseven Creek 150 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

flags.t: Route crosses private land (ParcelMap BC, updated 2026-09-27): get permission first or go around.

plan: Drive: from Resort Municipality of Whistler, about 195 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 51.20684, -121.73734, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 5.8 km S, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 243 m, about 141 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 200 m S of the spot at 1,481 m (51.15284, -121.74247). Water: Fiftyseven Creek right here (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 3-31, Region 3. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-27, closures 2026-10-16.
